title: Normalized blowup universal property and smooth comparison
statement:
Let $S$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $
u:S^
u	o S$ its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and $J\subset\mathcal O_S$ a coherent ideal whose zero scheme is nowhere dense. Write $B_J(S)=\operatorname{Bl}_J(S)^
u$, using the ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Then $B_J(S)$ is normal (its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]), reduced and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$. Its map to $S$ is surjective and birational on each component. It is the final normal $S$-scheme among morphisms taking generic points to generic points for which the extended ideal $J$ is invertible. In particular its only $S$-automorphism is the identity. There is a canonical identification over $S^
u$
$$B_J(S)\simeq B_{J\mathcal O_{S^
u}}(S^
u).$$
For every smooth $h:T	o S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with $T$ of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, $T$ is reduced and the canonical comparisons
$$T^
u\simeq S^
u	imes_S T,\qquad B_{J\mathcal O_T}(T)\simeq B_J(S)	imes_S T$$
are isomorphisms, and the induced map $B_{J\mathcal O_T}(T)	o B_J(S)$ is smooth. The extended ideal remains nowhere dense, and these comparisons respect identities and composition. Normalization is an isomorphism on a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. In particular, $B_{\mathcal O_S}(S)=S^
u$, and this equals $S$ when $S$ is normal.

source.place: Expose VIII, 2.2.1--2.2.4, Lemma 2.2.9 and 2.2.7--2.2.8, printed pp.89--91. Finiteness and normality of normalization: Stacks Tags 035S (morphisms.tex, lemma-nagata-normalization) and 035Q (morphisms.tex, lemma-normalization-normal), applied to finite-type Q-schemes. The input is one normalized blowup, with no resolution algorithm or equivariance assertion.

proof.text: Use the existing finiteness, normality, component-density and dense-preimage lemmas of ReducedAlgebraicNormalizationFieldChange, now public in their owning module. Blowup charts are subrings of localizations, hence reduced. The existing normal-locus theorem supplies a dense normal open of S. Intersect with the complement of the center, over which the blowup is an isomorphism. Normalization is an isomorphism there; density pulls back through the component normalizations. Properness plus the dense open gives surjectivity. This proves the geometric clauses.

Apply normalized-blowup finality for normality, generic domination, principalization and the mapping property. Apply it to endomorphisms to prove rigidity. For the unit center the ordinary blowup is an isomorphism; smooth normalization pullback identifies its normalization with that of S. Transport unit-center finality along this isomorphism to obtain the normalization mapping property.

A normal scheme is its componentwise normalization by integral normal generic recognition applied to the identity. For the lift from the normalized blowup to the normalization of S, apply the just-proved normalization mapping property. Its generic domination follows from the dense open normalization isomorphism. Finality on S and on its normalization gives the two inverse maps between the two normalized blowups; uniqueness proves both inverse equations.

A smooth map is flat and open, and geometric reducedness gives a reduced source; openness preserves the density of the complementary center. Flat blowup base change gives a pullback square for the ordinary blowups. Its upper map is smooth by base change. Apply smooth normalization pullback to that upper map and paste squares. Normalization and blowup finality identify every map with the map in these squares. Smoothness is stable under base change.

Generic points map to generic points under flat maps by the generalizing-map property. Composing these properties with those of normalized blowups makes finality apply to both the composite and direct comparison maps. Their structural equations agree, so uniqueness identifies them. Identity compatibility is the same argument. Equality elimination on centers produces exactly the displayed eqToHom casts. The normalization identities follow from unit-center finality.

A normal scheme is its own normalization by integral normal generic recognition. A regular scheme has domain, integrally closed stalks by the existing regular-scheme API. The unit-center isomorphism then also makes the unit normalized blowup structural map an isomorphism. All helper arguments permit the empty scheme.
